chunks: And in it, he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants in the distribution of reward.
But He is unjust to polytheism in the distribution of punishment.
ai.seo_question: How does divine justice apply differently to reward and punishment regarding polytheism?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this nuance to clarify that divine justice (*'adl*) does not imply uniform treatment for all sins, but rather proportional retribution based on the gravity of the offense. This rhetorical 'unjustice' toward *shirk* highlights its unique status as the ultimate violation of covenant, distinguishing it from the sins of monotheists who may receive greater leniency or expiation.
